scenes.headline: Claude models a street from a splat
scenes.sub: Two MCP servers, one loop, and its token bill
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Plumb! Today, how Claude can build a Blender street from a Gaussian splat.

scenes.text: One model looks at the splat through LichtFeld Studio's server, writes Blender Python through a second server, then compares its own result with the splat.
scenes.say: The model looks at the splat through one server. It writes Blender code through a second one. Then it compares its own result with the splat.

steps.say: The model asks LichtFeld for a render from a capture camera, and a picture comes back.
Then it writes Python, and Blender runs it, building boxes, roads and poles.
A viewport picture comes back from the same pose, and the model compares the two.

scenes.title: The loop, six moves
scenes.say: Load the capture. Look at the splat and the photos. Extract what code can measure. Build in Blender, then compare and edit.

scenes.title: What one picture costs
scenes.note: visual tokens per image, from the vision docs
scenes.say: Pictures are the budget. A full size frame costs about four thousand seven hundred tokens at the high resolution tier. A loop sends many.

scenes.label: Recovered at 40% floaters, noisiest cloud
scenes.say: In a toy, code fits the up axis and the box from the points. With forty percent floaters and the noisiest cloud, six of twelve cases still recover.

scenes.text: Let code measure what code can, and let the model judge pictures.
scenes.say: Let code measure what code can. Let the model judge the pictures.

recap: Two servers: one sees, one builds.
Each picture costs thousands of tokens.
scenes.say: Two servers, one loop, a big picture bill, and numbers from code.
